pr_title: fix: try catch `strict_equals` to avoid error accessing `STATE_SYMBOL`
pr_body:
## Svelte 5 rewrite

Closes #13214 

I'm not 100% sure with this fix but i don't think we can really do much here...it's a very niche case because you are trying to access something where you can't check if `STATE_SYMBOL` is there without causing trouble in the first place.

But since it's no harm i guess we can just try catch it. No test for the moment but i actually just thought of a way to test this so i'm gonna try to write a test.

Please note that [the Svelte codebase is currently being rewritten for Svelte 5](https://svelte.dev/blog/runes). Changes should target Svelte 5, which lives on the default branch (`main`).

If your PR concerns Svelte 4 (including updates to [svelte.dev.docs](https://svelte.dev/docs)), please ensure the base branch is `svelte-4` and not `main`.

### Before submitting the PR, please make sure you do the following

- [x] It's really useful if your PR references an issue where it is discussed ahead of time. In many cases, features are absent for a reason. For large changes, please create an RFC: https://github.com/sveltejs/rfcs
- [x] Prefix your PR title with `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, or `docs:`.
- [x] This message body should clearly illustrate what problems it solves.
- [ ] Ideally, include a test that fails without this PR but passes with it.

### Tests and linting

- [x] Run the tests with `pnpm test` and lint the project with `pnpm lint`

issue_context.title: Svelte 5: generated `strict_equals` causes cross-origin iframe SecurityError due to `get_proxied_value` attempting to read a property on a secure context
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

`SecurityError: Blocked a frame with origin "http://example.com" from accessing a cross-origin frame.`

Cross-origin frame violation error is triggered because svelte generates code for a simple non-reactive binary comparison `a===b` with `strict_equals(a, b)` which uses `get_proxied_value()` that tries accessing `STATE_SYMBOL in value` of an special secure property `iframe.contentWindow`.

Looking at REPL generated code, this generated equality check seems to be only present in dev mode.

These times I wish it was clearer in the docs how to prevent svelte from performing such checks where they're not needed. My current workaround is to use an outside comparison function just to avoid this case, which is a bit silly.

### Reproduction

https://svelte-5-preview.vercel.app/#H4sIAAAAAAAACnWQzWrDMBCEX0XsyYFg300USGluLT0ktJSqNIq8dkRlrZDWSYPxuxfbPZT-XBZm5pvDTg-1dZigfOnB6xahhE0IsAS-hlGkMzpGWEKiLprRWSUTbeC1QxZ11C2uii9H-ZWdHKG8YrbsUCpQMKqj9VXJJ5tkPyHDxKRopIITc0hlUeCHboPD3FCrYMrJO9KV7DM8o-eFXPejq7goRMbUNA7F7fZRGGqDdSgosCW_mBlDPrHQQoqpnJsuRvS817FBzg15Rs9P1ld0-V44Cjm_9R9CDnNHTaYXoijEheJ7-h0ef4Z_9KWUM7ZD00XL122MFEVmncNGO6GNwZQE1eKw22_227fd8_3Nw91h-m8YxjtOXsybr2EJLVW2tlhBybHD4XX4BHMfHhHeAQAA

```ts
const obj = {};
const st = $state(obj);
console.log(obj === st); // <-- not equal
```
